title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Devices Showing False Defender Antivirus Turned Off Warnings
content_md: Microsoft has confirmed a Windows notification defect that can falsely indicate to users that “Microsoft Defender Antivirus is turned off” even when the security product remains operational and its settings show that protection is enabled. The company says the incorrect alerts began appearing after installation of the latest Microsoft Defender Antivirus updates . The issue is notable because the message describes a condition that normally requires immediate attention: antivirus protection disabled. In this case, however, Microsoft states that Defender continues functioning correctly. The misleading notification may display during Windows startup and can reappear intermittently afterward, creating a recurring warning state on otherwise protected endpoints. Microsoft Confirms Windows Devices Showing False Defender Antivirus Microsoft also says the notifications persist even when users disable notification settings, limiting the common workaround and increasing the likelihood that administrators and end users will continue to see the alert. Microsoft’s advisory classifies the problem as confirmed. It was opened on August 28 at 15:34 Pacific Time, and last updated the same day at 16:02 PT; its status history contains no originating update. The scope spans supported client and server releases where Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running with the latest Defender updates.
